issues.claim: §2.7's support step (6) (a) (R4-09's text, l. 2586-2591) runs the support step once more after S7's batches 'with every obstacle then standing (S5b's and S5c's ways; S7's strips, gate plazas, castle paths, quays, piers and moles)', and 'a station this run can neither slide nor omit within `maxClearSpanM` and `maxPierM` keeps the place the earlier run gave it, and the S7 part it meets gives way in that batch — a strip, plaza or square cut round its ring, a quay, pier, mole or castle path ending at the ring and resuming beyond it'. The failure rung names S7's parts only. Where what such a station meets is a part-0 way — an S5b main road or an S5c street laid across an S4 or S5b viaduct at generation, which §4.3 *Lattice and costs* (l. 5629-5632) lets cross the strip wherever the soffit clears ('and the support step's last run (*The slot*, below) slides the supports off it ((6) (a))'), or S7's intervallum lane — nothing gives way: the station keeps its place in the way's corridor, a pier standing in a street (VEW-r3-01's impossible result, which R4-09 removes after generation), and §4.3 states the slide as always succeeding. Reachable: masonry `pierSpacingM` 8-15 m against `maxClearSpanM` 30 m (V11 §3.24.2), so a METROPOLIS `through` or `primary` way crossing a viaduct obliquely occupies 30 m or more of deck and the two stations in it can neither slide within `slideMaxFactor` nor be omitted; at generation no squareness bound applies. T110-2 (3)'s list (setback, glacis, berm, moat, gate plaza, quay, pier, mole) bars no way corridor.
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step (6) (a), after '… a quay, pier, mole or castle path ending at the ring and resuming beyond it — reported (`W_RAISED_CROSSING`).': 'Where such a station meets a part-0 way's corridor — an S5b or S5c way, or S7's intervallum lane — that way's crossing of the under-deck strip moves in that batch along the strip to the nearest place whose corridor clears every station, by §4.3's crossing shift (its vertices moved on ground part 0, the faces beside it following), reported (`W_RAISED_CROSSING`), so no pier stands in a way's corridor.' §4.3 *Lattice and costs* (pipeline's end): '… slides the supports off it ((6) (a))' → '… slides the supports off it, or, where a support can neither slide nor be omitted within its bounds, moves the way's crossing clear of it ((6) (a))'. §13.2's T110-2 (3) (scope's end): its list adds 'a way's corridor', with a METROPOLIS fixture whose S4 masonry viaduct a `through` way crosses obliquely over two stations: the way's crossing moved clear, reported, 0 piers in a way's corridor. (The adjudicator may rule another last rung — e.g. S5b's and S5c's ways keeping off the support rings at generation as after it, so the earlier run's place is always lawful — provided no pier stands in a way's corridor, no span or pier passes its bound and no course is dropped.)

issues.claim: §2.7's support step (6) (a) (l. 2591-2594; the model's judgment (3)) makes a locked or pinned raised way at a Re-derive 'crossed at generation as a standing one ((b)), and the run after S7 moves none of its stations, every S7 part one meets giving way'; §4.3 (l. 5624-5626: impassable 'at generation where the raised way is locked or pinned') and §4.4 S5a *Outer moats* (l. 5878-5879: 'across a locked or pinned raised way, the trace passes through its station') state the same branch. No bar exercises it: T110-2 (4) locks the raised way only for an epoch circuit and a hand `drawWall` (l. 18413-18418), T-V6-47 likewise; no fixture regenerates a stage trace across a locked raised way (the model's round-4 HAND-OFFS name it).
issues.required_change: §13.2's T110-2 adds '(6) a Re-derive from S4 of (1)'s c15 fixture with its S4 timber viaduct locked: stage 2's ring through one station on the deck at its level, the trace bent to it; no station moved, added or omitted and no key minted; the berm and channel passing under the deck only under `open` spans with no support, ramp, stair or foot in them, stopped at the under-deck strip's edges elsewhere (`W_RAISED_CROSSING`); after the last support run every S7 part a station meets cut round its ring or ended at it; 0 S5b or S5c way corridors over a support ring, ramp, stair or foot'.

issues.claim: §2.7's support step (6) (a) (l. 2582-2586) rules that where an S5a crossing cannot keep its bounds, or the berm or channel would meet a ramp, stair or foot, 'the stage's berm and channel — and S7's setback and glacis after them — are not laid under the deck: they stop at the edges of the under-deck strip … and the strip lines closed along it'. §4.4 S5a *Outer moats* states the berm-and-channel half; §4.8 *Wall strips, band, setbacks, intervallum* (l. 7595ff), which lays the setback and glacis lines, neither states the S7 half nor cites (6) (a) for it (§4.8's lead cites (6) (a) only for the last support run). Nothing built changes while §2.7 is read.
issues.required_change: §4.8 *Wall strips, band, setbacks, intervallum*, after the sentence defining the outer strip ('Outside: the band's half plus the outer setback and glacis …'): 'Where S5a stopped the stage's berm and channel at a raised way's under-deck strip (§2.7's support step (6) (a)), the setback and glacis lines stop there too, closed along the strip's edges, reported (`W_RAISED_CROSSING`).'

issues.claim: §5.4's `GenerationReport.stages[].warnings` comment (l. 9253) lists the stages' own non-kernel warning codes (S3's `W_WALLED_BY_BARRIERS` and `W_MOAT_DRY`, S10b's `W_DOSSIER_EDGE`, the underground's) but not `W_RAISED_CROSSING`, which §2.7's support step (6) (a) and §4.4 S5a *Outer moats* now issue at S5a and at S7's last support run (named in the model's round-4 HAND-OFFS).
issues.required_change: The comment adds "S5a's and S7's `W_RAISED_CROSSING` (§2.7's support step (6) (a); §4.4 *Outer moats*)".

issues.claim: §2.7's support step (6) (b) (l. 2596-2598, R4-09's text): 'only an op that names the raised way changes it (its edits, V06 §3.19's ops, a landfall, a frame growth's extension of its deck, §3.2 (9)), and none drops it'. Read as written, 'none' covers 'its edits', yet a hand delete of a raised way drops it (§7.1 *Delete*; §7.4's row, l. 11365: 'a removed generated one stays removed'; §2.7 *Source and lifecycle*: 'a removal of a generated way is a suppression'). The meaning R4-09 states is that nothing laid later drops it; the rows that build the delete are explicit, so nothing built changes.
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step (6) (b): 'and none drops it' → 'and no later work drops it'.

issues.claim: §4.3 *Lattice and costs* (l. 5629-5632) gives the generation regime 'At generation, before the span rule has run' (a later stage's way crosses an unlocked raised way's strip wherever the soffit clears), but §2.7's support step (6) (a) (l. 2577) runs the span rule on an S4 or S5b viaduct at a stage's S5a commit ('re-run (1)–(5), and then the span rule, on it in the same commit'), before that stage's S5c grows. Read literally, a stage-2 street crossing such a viaduct is no longer 'before the span rule has run', and §4.3 states no regime for a ruled span at generation (its open-span rule applies 'once generation has ended' or to a held raised way). §2.7's span rule has one eager time ('at the end of the raised way's generation (after §4.6's cut)', l. 2620), which (6) (a)'s last run cites.
issues.required_change: §4.3: 'At generation, before the span rule has run,' → 'At generation, until the span rule's eager run (after §4.6's cut, §2.7's span rule; a run at an S5a commit, §2.7's support step (6) (a), does not end it),'.
